title: "How This Ecosystem Works"

## Four Tools, One Workflow

This course uses four interconnected tools. Each one has a specific job. Here is where to go for what.

---

### Where to Find Things

| I need to... | Go here |
|---|---|
| Check the schedule or find an assignment description | **This website** (Open Methods Hub) |
| Open this week's workbook lab | **VS Code** (in your Methods Vault workspace) |
| Write a journal entry or organize notes | **VS Code** (the Methods Vault workspace) |
| Read the textbook | **[From Vibes to Variables](https://aura-lab-siue.github.io/v2v/)** (online) or in your workspace (`05_Textbook/`) |
| Run R code or render a document | **VS Code** |
| Submit an assignment | **Blackboard** |
| Push my work to my portfolio | **GitHub Desktop** |

---

### The Four Tools

**VS Code (Methods Vault)** is your personal workspace. You write journals, take literature notes, and organize your project here. Everything is Markdown, the same syntax you will use in R and Quarto later. Note-linking and backlinks come from the Foam extension, so you can connect notes with `[[wiki-links]]`, browse a backlinks panel, and view a graph of your notes. You start using VS Code in Week 1.

**v2v** is an R package you install once. It sets up your environment, checks that everything works, and provides sampled practice fixtures for the applied weeks. You install it in Week 2 and use it throughout the semester.

**From Vibes to Variables** is the textbook. You can read it online or in your workspace. It has 14 chapters covering the full research arc from curiosity to publication.

**This website (Open Methods Hub)** is your reference guide. It has the syllabus, the weekly schedule, setup instructions, and assignment descriptions. When you are not sure what is due or how to do something, check here first.

---

### The Weekly Rhythm

Each teaching week follows the same pattern:

1. **Read** the assigned chapter(s) in the textbook
2. **Open** the week's workbook lab in VS Code
3. **Work** through the lab in VS Code (depending on the week)
4. **Write** your journal entry in VS Code
5. **Push** your journal to GitHub using GitHub Desktop
6. **Submit** any assignments to Blackboard by the deadline

---

### How the Tools Connect

```
  You read the textbook
         |
         v
  You work in VS Code (journals, notes, qualitative work)
         |
         v
  You push to GitHub (builds your commit history)
         |
         v
  You work in VS Code (R assignments, data analysis)
         |
         v
  You render with Quarto (final portfolio: PDF + website)
         |
         v
  You publish to GitHub Pages (live portfolio URL)
         |
         v
  You submit to Blackboard (PDF + URL)
```

---

### When Each Tool Appears

| Weeks | Primary Tools |
|-------|--------------|
| 1 to 9 | VS Code, GitHub Desktop, Zotero, this website |
| 10 to 13 | VS Code, R, v2v (plus VS Code for journals) |
| 15 to 17 | Quarto, GitHub Pages (assembling the final portfolio) |

You do not need to learn everything at once. Each tool is introduced when you need it.
